description: Database password hardcoded as a literal container environment variable
note:
Was labelled empty, and is the number that moved. Neither tool reports a password typed straight into a manifest, and the direction is backwards: the CORRECT form (valueFrom.secretKeyRef) raises CKV_K8S_35, while this, the dangerous form, raised nothing. IACP-0002 (lambda/iac-scanner/checks/) is this project's check for it, added 2026-09-20 the same way IACP-0001 closed the port-range gap.

The upstream cause is structural and specific to Kubernetes. checkov's secret detection is EntropyKeywordCombinator: a keyword must combine with a detect-secrets entropy hit on the value. In a Secret's stringData the two are one YAML pair and CKV_SECRET_6 fires -- see the sibling case k8s-literal-secret-in-secret-object, which carries the identical value. In a container's env list the keyword is under `name:` and the secret under `value:`, two separate keys, so they are never paired. Shape-matched credentials are unaffected: an AKIA... key here fires CKV_SECRET_2, because AWSKeyDetector needs no keyword. The value is base64-charset only so this does not also trip the punctuation gap rds-literal-password isolates.
